id="1" parent="0" /> <mxCell id="9IURa8MdqJPCk-QmwCEp-1" value="<h1 data-end="162" data-start="99"><strong data-end="162" data-start="101">Single-Node vs Multi-Node Architecture&nbsp;</strong></h1><br><div class="_tableContainer_1rjym_1"><div class="group _tableWrapper_1rjym_13 flex w-fit flex-col-reverse" tabindex="-1"><table class="w-fit min-w-(--thread-content-width)" data-end="1565" data-start="164"><thead data-end="229" data-start="164"><tr data-end="229" data-start="164"><th data-col-size="sm" data-end="175" data-start="164">Category</th><th data-col-size="md" data-end="202" data-start="175">Single-Node Architecture</th><th data-col-size="md" data-end="229" data-start="202">Multi-Node Architecture</th></tr></thead><tbody data-end="1565" data-start="298"><tr data-end="422" data-start="298"><td data-col-size="sm" data-end="315" data-start="298"><strong data-end="314" data-start="300">Deployment</strong></td><td data-end="365" data-start="315" data-col-size="md">Everything runs on one server.</td><td data-end="422" data-start="365" data-col-size="md">Components distributed across multiple servers/nodes.</td></tr><tr data-end="508" data-start="423"><td data-col-size="sm" data-end="441" data-start="423"><strong data-end="440" data-start="425">Scalability</strong></td><td data-end="468" data-start="441" data-col-size="md">Limited (vertical only).</td><td data-end="508" data-start="468" data-col-size="md">High (horizontal scaling supported).</td></tr><tr data-end="634" data-start="509"><td data-col-size="sm" data-end="538" data-start="509"><strong data-end="537" data-start="511">Performance Under Load</strong></td><td data-end="579" data-start="538" data-col-size="md">Slows down quickly with heavy traffic.</td><td data-end="634" data-start="579" data-col-size="md">Load distributed across nodes → better performance.</td></tr><tr data-end="759" data-start="635"><td data-col-size="sm" data-end="657" data-start="635"><strong data-end="656" data-start="637">Fault Tolerance</strong></td><td data-end="697" data-start="657" data-col-size="md">No redundancy; failure = full outage.</td><td data-end="759" data-start="697" data-col-size="md">High redundancy; one node failure does not impact service.</td></tr><tr data-end="876" data-start="760"><td data-col-size="sm" data-end="779" data-start="760"><strong data-end="778" data-start="762">Availability</strong></td><td data-end="827" data-start="779" data-col-size="md">Low; downtime during failures or maintenance.</td><td data-end="876" data-start="827" data-col-size="md">High; supports HA, failover, rolling updates.</td></tr><tr data-end="998" data-start="877"><td data-col-size="sm" data-end="895" data-start="877"><strong data-end="894" data-start="879">Maintenance</strong></td><td data-end="940" data-start="895" data-col-size="md">Easier to manage but causes full downtime.</td><td data-end="998" data-start="940" data-col-size="md">Complex, but maintenance can be done without downtime.</td></tr><tr data-end="1103" data-start="999"><td data-col-size="sm" data-end="1014" data-start="999"><strong data-end="1013" data-start="1001">Security</strong></td><td data-end="1040" data-start="1014" data-col-size="md">Smaller attack surface.</td><td data-end="1103" data-start="1040" data-col-size="md">Larger attack surface; requires stronger security controls.</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>" style="text;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=23;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="38" y="50" width="1119"
